commentary_text:
There is a warm crosswind at South Meridian Institute Ground, and Shoreline Rangers begin with the television director already warning that the scoring ribbon is taking numbers from a live scorer and a delayed graphics cache. Finn Archer drives the first loose ball and keeps most of the strike while Leo Marsh settles. A glance off the pad is initially entered to Finn. The umpire is partly hidden behind Leo, so the booth carries Finn's opening-stand contribution as forty. No correction appears before the next over. The old figure also goes into the wagon-wheel thumbnail, where it will survive longer than the live commentary. Nothing about this early panel can yet be treated as a closed personal total.

Leo's own innings ends at 8.4 when he is caught by Aiden Scott from Zane Cooper. The board behind the bowler has Shoreline on sixty-two for one. Two byes have already been signalled during the opening passage, but they are mentioned only in an exchange about the keeper's footwork. Rory Blake comes in, blocks his first ball, and loses off stump to Zane on the next. The score has not moved between the wickets. The new batter waits at the rope while the director shows Rory's dismissal from behind the arm, then from square leg. A feed process logs the second view as another item even though it contains the same batter, delivery and wicket state.

Miles Carter walks out after Rory. The innings is now sixty-two for two, a state shown only on the sightscreen. Finn and Miles settle through singles and a late cut. Finn's contribution inside this association reaches thirty-six on the provisional stand card, but Miles's share and the extras box are absent from that picture. The second angle of Rory's wicket returns while the pair are batting. It remains an archival view: there was no run during Rory's stay, and the new partnership is already under way.

Dylan Vale is padded up when the camera catches a scoring argument near the boundary. Five extras have accumulated during the Finn-Miles association. A timing marker appears to have crossed the coming wicket boundary, yet the operator queues the repair without saying which personal panel will change. The main ribbon disappears before either batter's settled contribution is shown. Miles is later caught by Julian Vale from Aiden Scott, while a cropped caption saying only “Miles caught” creates a surname trap for the interval bowling montage.

Dylan Vale begins with four runs in the brief passage before Finn's dismissal. Miles Benton finds Finn's edge, and Arin Wells completes the catch. This is a valid Benton dismissal, although no running wicket total is attached to his name. The camera replays the edge twice from different angles. Those pictures describe one departure. The broadcaster does not disclose whether Finn added anything after Miles Carter left; that small component remains unresolved until the closing archive review.

Only after Finn has left does the scorer settle the opening pad incident. The side-on picture shows no bat, and the missed signal is confirmed as a leg bye. The team total is untouched. Finn's opening contribution therefore becomes one lower than the forty first shown. The graphics cache keeps the old number in an archival panel, but the live contribution ledger changes. This correction is separated from the Finn-Miles boundary repair: one concerns attribution in the opening stand, the other concerns a run placed after Miles's wicket. Treating them as the same repair would lose the evidence needed to close Finn's innings.

Dylan begins a longer rebuild with Connor Wells. A quick single is placed against Dylan, taking his provisional contribution in this stand to fourteen. Several overs later, during a crowd shot, the scorer receives a low replay showing that the ball brushed the pad without touching the bat. The missed leg-bye signal moves one unit out of Dylan's column. Connor is eventually bowled by Zane Cooper with a ball that also moves into off stump. It resembles Rory's dismissal in wording and camera angle, yet the other batter is Dylan, the innings is much further advanced, and the partnership state is different. Connor's wicket is therefore a new event for Zane, while the second Rory angle remains a replay.

Evan Price joins Dylan next. Dylan's provisional contribution reaches ten before Aiden Scott bowls Evan. The final single displayed in that component occurs during a transition in which Noah Grant is already approaching the middle. The scorer marks the stand boundary for later review but does not change the number here. The dismissal later appears among several straight balls hitting the stumps, beside Zane Cooper's earlier wickets. Aiden's shirt and the over graphic keep Evan outside Zane's ledger.

Noah Grant gives Dylan the longest late stay. Dylan supplies thirty-seven in their association before Benton has him caught by Isaac Vale. The director later runs this catch beside Finn's and Miles Carter's, but the full delivery view preserves each bowler. Dylan's personal card is deliberately withheld as he walks; only the Noah-stand share is visible. His earlier contributions and both pending attribution questions remain on different feeds, so no displayed number can be repaired by a single decrement to obtain the innings row.

Aaron Miles comes in near the end and Benton bowls him, a distinct dismissal with a different mode from the catches. During the walk-off, an old Finn-Miles partnership tile appears in the corner and shows Miles Carter's contribution as thirty-seven. It is provisional because the boundary timing dispute has not yet been applied to that batter. A few deliveries later Logan Shaw also loses his stumps, but Cameron Ellis is bowling. An interval edit places the two bowled dismissals together; the live calls keep Aaron with Benton and Logan with Cameron.

Elsewhere at the scorer's table, the batting subtotal has reached two hundred sixty-two. It includes a personal run in both a pending correction record and the settled batting ledger. The operator removes the duplicate, leaving the batter aggregate one lower. This adjustment is not paired on screen with the extras categories. The producer instead returns to the replay of Finn's edge, and the scoreboard box disappears. The repaired batting subtotal will need to be combined later with evidence from several different parts of the broadcast; no completed innings number is supplied here.

A no-ball during Noah's partnership forces the bowler to reset his run-up. Several deliveries later Noah is caught from Benton's bowling, but the television loses the bowler panel during a camera reset. The live call and batter identity preserve the link. In a separate scorer message, the last unit of Dylan's earlier Evan Price component is moved beyond Evan's wicket into the Noah partnership. Dylan's provisional ten in the Evan stand therefore loses one. This second personal correction is independent of the Connor-stand leg bye and occurs many overs later.

The wides ledger for Shoreline first reaches eighteen. One entry comes from a feed refresh rather than an umpire's signal: the bowler is already walking back, the striker has not changed, and the ball identifier matches the preceding wide. The scorer flags the second entry but does not remove it immediately. The feed does not place the repaired wide beside any other extras category or the batting subtotal.

Miles Carter's dismissal state is shown again during an analysis break: Shoreline had reached one hundred thirty-eight for three when he was caught. The analyst discusses field pressure and does not replay the lower wicket state, either settled batter share or the extras box. A small scorer note confirms only that Finn's provisional stand component must lose the run placed beyond Miles's dismissal. Miles's own pending boundary repair remains unresolved.

The scorer removes the refreshed wide, leaving that category one below eighteen. During another feed change, Miles Carter's old partnership contribution is also reduced by the run that belonged after his wicket. These corrections affect different ledgers and are not displayed beside the partnership's start or end state. Logan Shaw later becomes Shoreline's tenth distinct batter dismissed when Cameron Ellis bowls him after forty-seven completed overs and two further legal balls.

Meridian Strikers start the chase with Arin Wells taking the only run before Isaac Vale is lbw to Caleb Turner at 0.4. The first-wicket state is one for one. Caleb's over eventually contributes six wides to his bowling sheet, though those wides occur across his spell and are not part of this first wicket. The director previews Isaac's dismissal twice during a break. Both previews belong to Caleb and to the chase, so neither can be imported into Zane's first-innings ledger. Arin's single remains his first personal contribution.

Evan Carter joins Arin. Evan contributes seven in their stand, while the stand-extras panel provisionally opens at seven. Arin's share is hidden when the graphic freezes, so the replay caption contains only Evan and extras. No wicket-state boundary is visible. Finn Archer later sends one wide during his short spell, while Logan Shaw's sheet records none. The keeper also notes that the chase has produced no byes, a category fact displayed without the partnership panel.

Tyler Quinn arrives after Evan and shares an eighteen-run association with Arin. Arin contributes ten, but Tyler's share is not shown in this segment. A possible pad contact prompts discussion without an immediate ruling. Connor Reed's bowling sheet will eventually contain two wides, and the earlier wide in his over does not consume a legal delivery. The broadcast moves to a field-setting interview before either Tyler's attribution or Arin's earlier Carter-stand share is settled.

A delayed feed check for the Carter-Arin stand arrives during a sightscreen interruption. One delivery had generated both a live wide call and an automatic duplicate. The duplicated unit is removed from the stand extras, taking that component one below its provisional seven. Arin's personal attribution is not repaired on this feed; it is sent to a separate queue. The team score loses the phantom feed entry once, and the old replay caption remains archival.

Evan's innings ends when Logan Shaw bowls him at 6.2. Only now does the main board show Meridian at twenty-seven for two. The stand had begun from the first-wicket state several paragraphs earlier, while Evan's share, Arin's provisional share and the extras correction were each supplied separately. The dismissal gives a distant upper boundary. Aaron Miles's bowling figures are not involved, even though an Aaron graphic briefly appears as the next field setting is discussed.

A cached Tyler panel appears after Arin has left and gives Tyler seven for the completed Arin partnership. The scorer has not yet applied the pad-contact review, so that component remains provisional. Much later Tyler is caught by Dylan Vale from Aaron Miles, creating Aaron's first credited dismissal in the chase. The catch closes Tyler's opportunity to add in subsequent stands, but his personal contribution with Aiden Scott and the earlier pad ruling are still absent from this segment.

The chase-wide ribbon is provisionally at thirteen because a legal dot remains after a refresh. Aaron Miles's bowling sheet separately carries two wides. On another monitor, Arin's contribution in the Evan Carter partnership finally appears as fourteen, still carrying the attribution tied to the duplicated feed item. The scorer marks that personal panel for review but does not alter it while the weather graphic remains on screen.

Blake Morgan is bowled by Aaron Miles several overs after Tyler's catch. Earlier in the over an umpire had called the chase's single no-ball, but that extra is not shown beside the dismissal. The big screen then replays Tyler's catch. Blake is already walking and the next batter is taking guard, so the crowd's second reaction cannot create another Aaron wicket. No cumulative bowling numeral is displayed.

Arin's dismissal is delivered by Connor Reed. Before Arin falls, only Isaac and Evan have completed dismissal events in the chase. The Tyler-Arin stand had added eighteen to the score established at Evan's wicket. A post-wicket graphic later shows forty-six for three, but its score component still includes the Carter-stand feed duplicate. The scorer does not repair that strip in this paragraph, and the over position is not displayed with it. The graphic is retained as a provisional state rather than a final fall-of-wickets entry.

Leo Foster is bowled by Aaron Miles much later, after Julian Vale has been dismissed by Connor Reed and Aiden Scott has fallen to Tyler Quinn. Those intervening wickets prevent the Aaron events from forming one uninterrupted ledger. The director shows Leo's ball live and then in slow motion. A production counter treats the slow-motion view as fresh, but the batter, delivery and wicket state are identical. The duplicate remains pending rather than being immediately cancelled.

The camera follows the new pair after Leo's dismissal. Miles Benton and Cameron Ellis add a few uneasy runs while fielders crowd the bat. An earlier batting replay now shows that Tyler had contributed seven alongside Aiden Scott; it does not show Tyler's still-provisional share with Arin. Tyler Quinn's completed bowling sheet appears during the pause and contains one wide, a dispersed check on the chase extras. Aaron is off screen and no dismissal is added to his column here.

The legal-ball detail for Arin's wicket arrives in a later review. Eleven full overs had been completed, and Connor's wicket ball was the fourth legitimate delivery beyond them. A wide earlier in the over did not advance that count. During the same review, Arin's provisional Carter-stand contribution is repaired: the duplicated feed unit is removed, leaving that component one below fourteen. His opening single and Tyler-stand contribution are not repeated.

The legal dot retained as a chase wide is finally removed, leaving that ledger one below thirteen. The scorer does not place the other extras categories beside it. A replay of Aiden Scott's dismissal follows; Tyler Quinn, not Aaron Miles, was the bowler. This intervening wicket is retained as a real event and prevents a strategy that assigns every late dismissal to Aaron.

Cameron Ellis later advances to a flighted ball from Aaron Miles, and Owen Hayes removes the bails with Cameron short. The batting dismissal, partnership end and fall-of-wickets feed accept the stumping immediately. Aaron's bowling summary does not, leaving this genuine event absent from his provisional column. The correction is deferred while the broadcast revisits the previous partnership, so it is not adjacent to the slow-motion duplicate of Leo.

The closing scoring sweep performs several separated repairs. Cameron's stumping is propagated into Aaron's bowling column because it came from a legal delivery; the slow-motion copy of Leo's wicket is removed without disturbing Leo's actual dismissal. On a different screen, Tyler's pad review is finally settled. One unit leaves his provisional Arin-stand contribution for leg byes. The separately reported Aiden-stand contribution remains unchanged and is not repeated here.

An archival first-innings clip then resolves two old gaps without displaying totals. During the brief Finn-Dylan stand, Dylan made the four already reported while Finn added nothing. A separate partnership correction shows Miles Carter's provisional thirty-seven losing the run placed beyond his dismissal; it does not repeat Finn's share, the five extras or either wicket boundary. Finn's personal ledger and the partnership ledger therefore close from evidence separated across the opening, middle and final broadcast sections.

The programme ends with a consistency sweep that avoids completed answers. Shoreline's repaired batter ledger is checked against dispersed extras categories, wicket identity and legal-ball state on separate screens. Meridian's extras and partnership records are checked against evidence shown at different stages of the chase. The montage repeats several wickets from both innings without advancing state. Unique event identity, delayed attribution and innings scope remain the only reliable path through the cached panels.
